# GitTurtle patch to gpui-pre-linux 0.3.4

This directory contains the exact crates.io `gpui-pre-linux` 0.3.4 source under Apache-2.0, the version the matching GPUI Kit 0.6.0 stack locks. `LICENSE-APACHE` is byte-for-byte preserved. The registry archive (`gpui-pre-linux-0.3.4.crate`) has SHA-256 `8fd1d912c039641f0236b1701b7871bfddfb4926ffd1915b3958b73d03177250`, the checksum the workspace lockfile recorded for it; the package metadata names Zed's `crates/gpui_linux` at `69164008341295ad481bb11c0334a712ca8c23e3` (`https://github.com/zed-industries/zed`). `Cargo.toml` is the published normalized manifest and `Cargo.toml.orig` the original one; dependency requirements are unchanged and the workspace lockfile pins their versions. The registry-only `.cargo-ok` and the package lockfile are omitted. Apart from this note, `src/linux/wayland/window.rs` is the only file that differs from the archive.

Cargo stops checking the archive checksum once the crate comes from a path, so compare the tree with the archive it came from when reviewing a change here:

```sh
mkdir -p .local/gpui-pre-linux-archive
tar xzf ~/.cargo/registry/cache/index.crates.io-*/gpui-pre-linux-0.3.4.crate -C .local/gpui-pre-linux-archive
diff -r --exclude=Cargo.lock --exclude=GITTURTLE-PATCH.md .local/gpui-pre-linux-archive/gpui-pre-linux-0.3.4 vendor/gpui-pre-linux
```

The crate is the Linux and FreeBSD platform backend; its dependencies are all under `cfg(any(target_os = "linux", target_os = "freebsd"))`, so the macOS build graph does not reach it.

## Change: Wayland text input only while a text field is focused

This is a runtime change to the Wayland backend, a backport of upstream [zed-industries/zed#63776](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/63776) (fixing [#63774](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/issues/63774)), first released in `gpui-pre` 0.3.5. It leaves the X11 and headless backends unchanged. The decision and its evidence are in [the 2026-11-03 decision record](../../docs/development/2026-11-03-wayland-text-input-focus.md).

`WaylandWindowStatePtr::update_ime_enabled`, which runs after every frame of an active window, decides whether the window keeps the text-input protocol (`zwp_text_input_v3`) on. With a focused input handler it asks the handler whether it accepts text input; with none, 0.3.4 answered `true`, so text input stayed on for every button, menu, list and shortcut. With text input on, an input method such as fcitx5, as on a default Omarchy, takes the keyboard: it delivers a held key as a release and a fresh press at the seat's repeat rate, each `is_held: false`, so GPUI's own repeat timer (`wayland/client.rs`), which marks repeats held, never runs, and it swallows single-letter shortcuts outside text fields. A key held on a toolbar dropdown reopened its menu about 72 times in 2 s (native probes QA-90 and QA-91).

The decision now lives in a pure function, `text_input_enabled(Option<bool>)`, given `None` when no handler is focused and the handler's answer otherwise: text input is on only for `Some(true)`, a focused handler that accepts text input. The kit's text input registers a handler while it is focused and accepts text input while editable, so the commit message, the palette and other fields keep the input method, with composition and candidate windows; read-only text, buttons, menus, lists and shortcuts get GPUI's own key events and held repeats. Dead keys and compose sequences come from xkb compose, not from text input, so they still work outside a text field. `update_ime_enabled` still only enables or disables the protocol when the answer changes.

A known transient, left as upstream has it: the text-input `Enter` event (`wayland/client.rs`, the `zwp_text_input_v3::Event::Enter` arm), sent when the surface gains keyboard focus, enables text input unconditionally, and it stays on until the window's next frame calls `update_ime_enabled` again, which turns it off when no text field is focused. Keys pressed in that gap, before the first frame after the window regains focus, still reach the input method.

Test: `linux::wayland::window::text_input_tests::text_input_follows_a_focused_text_field` checks the truth table (no handler: off; a handler accepting text input: on; a handler not accepting it: off), run with `scripts/vendor-crate-test.sh vendor/gpui-pre-linux`; it fails when the no-handler answer goes back to `true`. The GPUI test platform has no Wayland, so the protocol itself is checked natively under `WAYLAND_DEBUG=1` against the integrated build: focus on a dropdown logs `zwp_text_input_v3.disable` and a 2 s held Enter gives one press and one menu; focus in a field logs `enable` and fcitx5 Pinyin composes in the commit message and the palette; after Alt-Tab back with a button focused, text input stays disabled.

## Change: the window's content reaches the drawable's last device pixel

This is a GitTurtle runtime change to the Wayland backend, not an upstream backport. The decision is recorded in `docs/development/omarchy-full-support.md` (FU47-A, 2026-11-11): a window paints its last device pixel at every scale, and the fix belongs to the backend every surface shares, not to one page.

0.3.4 reported a window's content size, the size GPUI lays the root out at, as the surface's logical size, while it sized the drawable (the wgpu surface) by rounding that size times the scale half away from zero (`Size::to_device_pixels`). GPUI's layout rounds every edge half toward zero (`round_to_device_pixel`, `gpui-pre` `util.rs`), so where a side falls on half a device pixel the drawable rounded up and the root down: at 461 × 490 and scale 1.5 the drawable is 692 device pixels wide and the root, and with it every full-width quad and the window's own background, ended at 691; at 1.25 the drawable is 613 tall and the root ended at 612. The last device pixel column or row was never painted, and the root's content mask clipped it.

The drawable's size is now one pure function, `drawable_size(size, scale)`, used when the renderer is created (at the state's initial scale, 1, where 0.3.4 truncated instead) and on every resize and rescale (`WaylandWindowStatePtr::set_size_and_scale`), and the content size is `content_size_at(size, scale)`, that drawable size divided by the scale: 461.33 px at 1.5 and 490.4 px at 1.25, whose edges GPUI lays out on the drawable's last device pixel. The content differs from the surface's logical size by at most half a device pixel. The surface's logical size stays in `bounds()`, `window_bounds()` and `inner_window_bounds()`, in the xdg window geometry (`window_geometry`, which popup positioners anchor to), in the viewport destination and in the size handed to the resize callback, which GPUI ignores: each of those is what the protocol takes in integer surface coordinates, and none sets the root's layout.

The consumers of the content size were checked against the drawable after the change. GPUI's `Window` reads it on creation and in `bounds_changed` (every resize, rescale and move) as `viewport_size`, which sets the root's layout size, the root content mask, tooltip placement inside the window and the test for a drag leaving the window; the application's `views::body_bounds` and the status bar derive from `viewport_size`, and the kit's window border lays its client-decoration frame out inside the root. The kit's resize hit zones and the resize edge a press starts (`window_border.rs`) read `window_bounds()`, the surface's logical size, in the pointer's own coordinates, so they stay where the compositor's window geometry is, at most half a device pixel inside the frame's laid-out edge; only an untiled client-decorated window has them. Pointer positions, hit testing and the text-input cursor rectangle (`get_ime_area`, sent as `set_cursor_rectangle`) stay in surface-local logical coordinates, which map to device pixels by the same scale as before, so a pointer meets the same element at the same device pixel; the content now reaches the device pixel it lies in at the window's right side or foot. Popups and layer-shell surfaces are `WaylandWindow`s and take the same rule; their placement still comes from the parent's integer window geometry.

The X11 backend already reports the drawable's size over the scale: `set_bounds` divides the device size of each `ConfigureNotify` by the scale, the drawable is that window's own device geometry (`query_render_extent`), a new window is created at its bounds' device size and its state keeps that size over the scale, and its scale is fixed for the connection. XWayland at a fractional scale (an X11 client given 1.25 or 1.5 through `GPUI_X11_SCALE_FACTOR`, `Xft.dpi` or RandR) takes that path, so it is unchanged. The headless backend has no drawable and a fixed scale of 1, so it is unchanged too.

Tests: `linux::wayland::window::content_size_tests::the_root_reaches_the_drawables_last_device_pixel` lays out a full-width, full-height quad at 461 × 490 and scales 1.25 and 1.5 as GPUI rounds edges and checks, in device pixels, that its right and bottom edges are the drawable's (576 × 613 and 692 × 735); `the_root_reaches_the_drawable_at_every_size_and_scale` does so for every side from 1 to 4096 px at every scale the fractional-scale protocol gives from 1 to 3 (multiples of 1/120), and checks the content stays within half a device pixel of the surface. Both fail when `content_size_at` returns the surface's logical size again. Run them with `scripts/vendor-crate-test.sh vendor/gpui-pre-linux content_size_tests`. GPUI's test platform does not reach this backend, so the application's `views::tests::simulate_window_at_scale` sizes a test window as this function does, and `views::tests::a_window_paints_its_last_device_pixel_at_every_scale` checks that the application's background and status bar end on the drawable's last column and row there. That helper copies this arithmetic rather than calling it, so it passes with this change reverted: only `content_size_tests` guards the backend, and a change to its rounding must change the helper with it. Native evidence is a frame at the fractional scale.

Keep this change across an upgrade until upstream's Wayland `content_size` reports the drawable's size over the scale, as `content_size_tests` shows.

## Removing the patch

Remove the text-input change on an upgrade to `gpui-pre` 0.3.5 or later, which carries the upstream fix. Remove this patch, the `[patch.crates-io]` entry, the workspace exclusion, the `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` row and the `vendor/AGENTS.md` row only once upstream carries both changes.
